text:
lolPing 

 
 English 简体中文 
 

 
 League of Legends pings and emotes for your whole desktop, on Windows and macOS, and experimentally on Linux. 
 Hold Alt ( ⌥ Option on a Mac), drag, and let go on a ping. The animation pops and the sound plays on top of any app, on any monitor. 
 Hold Ctrl ( ⌃ Control on a Mac) and drag for the emote wheel: League's emotes, or your own images. 
 Turn on the AI teammate and ping anything with Win ( ⌘ ) to have a model or a coding agent answer at that spot.
 

 
 Download for Windows ·
 Download for Mac (Apple Silicon, experimental)
 

 
 
 
 
 

 

Pings and emotes show up in whole-screen capture, so friends watching your Discord or OBS stream see them too. lolPing is a desktop toy: it doesn't read, change or hook into League itself.

 Linux (experimental)

lolPing runs on Linux x64 in X11 and Wayland sessions, as an AppImage or a .deb . Alt + drag and Ctrl + drag work as on Windows. Caps Lock triggers and automatic fullscreen-game detection are not available, and the AI teammate is off.

- X11: nothing to set up.
- Wayland: the input helper reads /dev/input and passes your input on through /dev/uinput . The .deb sets up that access when it installs. For the AppImage, lolPing shows a Set up button the first time (it asks for your password once), or you can run the command it shows.
- Build: Node.js 22.12+, a C++20 compiler and libx11-dev libxi-dev libxtst-dev , then npm ci and npm run dist:linux . On Debian and Ubuntu, sudo apt install ./release/lolPing- -amd64.deb installs the package.
- Privacy: on Wayland the helper reads keyboard and mouse input on your computer to see wheel gestures. It doesn't save it and nothing leaves the computer.

See Linux build, installation and testing instructions for the limits (touchpads, remote desktop, Flatpak), desktop shortcut conflicts, tray requirements, HiDPI behaviour and manual updates.

 Install

 Windows

1. Download lolPing-Setup- .exe from the latest release.
2. Run it. The installer isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Select More info , then Run anyway .
3. lolPing opens its settings and moves to the tray. Hold Alt and drag anywhere to ping.

lolPing is built for Windows 11, 64-bit. Windows 10 may work, but it isn't tested.

 Portable (no install)

Download lolPing- -portable.exe instead and run it from any folder, including a USB drive. It keeps its settings, emotes and caches in a data folder next to the .exe , so nothing is written to %APPDATA% or the registry. Two things differ from the installed version: it doesn't update itself (download the next version from the releases page and replace the .exe ; the data folder carries over), and it can't launch at startup. The portable .exe unpacks to a temp folder on every start, so it opens a second or two slower than the installed version.

A portable and an installed lolPing can run at the same time, each with its own settings. To make an unpacked copy (the release/win-unpacked folder of a npm run dist ) portable, put an empty file named portable.txt next to lolPing.exe .

 macOS (experimental)

The Mac version needs an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) and macOS 13 or later. It is built and tested automatically, but hasn't had much use on real Macs yet. Please report anything that doesn't work.

1. Download lolPing- -arm64.dmg from the latest release, open it, and drag lolPing into Applications.
2. Open lolPing. It isn't signed by a registered Apple developer, so macOS says it can't check it for malware. Select Done , open System Settings → Privacy & Security , scroll down, select Open Anyway next to the lolPing message, and confirm.
 If macOS instead says lolPing "is damaged", run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/lolPing.app in Terminal and open it again.
3. lolPing asks for Accessibility access, which it needs to read the mouse and keyboard. Select Open System Settings and turn lolPing on. Pinging starts as soon as it's allowed.
4. lolPing lives in the menu bar. Hold ⌥ Option and drag anywhere to ping.

 After every update , macOS forgets the Accessibility permission, because the app isn't signed with a fixed developer identity. In Privacy & Security → Accessibility , select lolPing, remove it with – , then turn it on again. The settings window walks you through it.

 Updating an older version

Updating from v0.4 or earlier: download the new version by hand once. From v0.5 on, lolPing updates itself (see Updates).

 Use

 To Do this 
 --- --- 
 Ping Hold Alt , drag, and let go on a slice 
 Emote Hold Ctrl , drag, and let go on an emote 
 Cancel Let go in the centre, right-click, or press Esc 
 Pause or resume pinging Ctrl + Alt + P 
 Type a line to the room (in a room) Alt + T , type, then press Enter 
 Show who is in the room (in a room) Hold Tab 
 Ask the AI teammate (when it's on) Hold Win , drag, and let go on a ping over what you're asking about 
 Ask the teammate in your own words Win + click 
 Open settings Click the tray icon 
 Quit, or restart the input helper Right-click the tray icon 

On a Mac, use ⌥ Option instead of Alt, ⌃ Control instead of Ctrl for emotes, ⌘ instead of Win to ask (double-tap ⌘ to ask in words), ⌃⌥P to pause, and the ping icon in the menu bar instead of the tray icon.

The wheel, from the top going clockwise: Danger, Push, On My Way, All In, Assist Me, Need Vision, Enemy Missing, Enemy Vision. You can rearrange it and add Bait, Vision Cleared or an upside-down Enemy Missing ("¿") in settings. The emote wheel has 8 slots too, and you pick its emotes in settings. Each imported image plays its own signature effect (a spin, a bounce, a heartbeat...), picked by right-clicking it in the settings window from a grid where every effect plays live on that image.

 Settings

 

- Trigger key: Alt, Ctrl, Shift, Win, Caps Lock, Mouse 4, Mouse 5 or any other key (on a Mac: Option, Control, Shift, Command, Mouse 4, Mouse 5 or any other key). A custom key still types when tapped, but its let
